subject_line: Your brain went quiet and nobody warned you
opening: Happy Sunday, friends. This week we've got something a little strange, a little practical, and one article that your doctor probably hasn't read yet. Grab your coffee and let's get into it.

hero.title: Food Noise Went Quiet and Nobody Warned You
hero.teaser: You've heard the term food noise borrowed straight from the Ozempic conversation, and you probably nodded along thinking you knew what losing it would feel like. But community members who've been through it describe something much weirder than just 'not being hungry anymore.' The quiet, it turns out, can feel disorienting in ways nobody prepares you for. Chloe digs into what actually happens when it finally stops, and why your reaction might surprise you.

supporting.title: Carnivore With Health Conditions and Medications: A Guide
supporting.teaser: Sarah explains why blood pressure and blood sugar can shift faster than your doctor expects, and what to do before your numbers catch your prescription off guard.

supporting.title: Tuna and Eggs Only: Does This Reset Actually Work?
supporting.teaser: Marcus tested the reset everyone keeps posting about, and the one fix nobody mentions might be the reason yours didn't stick.

supporting.title: Losing Your Appetite on Carnivore: Warning or Win?
supporting.teaser: Sarah lays out the exact signs that tell you whether week four's missing hunger is your body thriving or quietly running on empty.

try_this_week: Before your next doctor's visit, write down every medication you take and the dose. If you're on blood pressure or blood sugar meds, bring that list and mention you're eating a very low carb diet. Sarah's guide this week gives you the specific questions worth asking so you're not caught off guard by a reading that shifted faster than expected.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something a lot of long-termers don't talk about openly, and the answer might change how you think about staying carnivore for good.
